sentences: I measure the yarn label to confirm the recommended needle size and gauge before starting the project.
I cast on sixty stitches using the long-tail method and then count them twice to be sure.
I knit the first row, then purl the second, alternating to create a stockinette fabric.
I check my gauge by knitting a four-inch square and counting the stitches per inch.
I read the pattern chart row by row, marking each completed row with a pencil.
I place a stitch marker at the beginning of the round to track where each round starts.
I increase one stitch at each end of the row by knitting into the front and back of the first and last stitches.
I decrease by knitting two stitches together at the marked positions to shape the armhole.
I make a yarn over between two stitches to create an eyelet hole in the lace pattern.
I slip the next three stitches onto a cable needle and hold them in front while I knit the following three.
I change to a contrasting color and carry the unused strand along the back of the work.
I count the remaining stitches on my needle after finishing each section to match the pattern.
I rip out several rows back to the mistake, then pick up the live stitches again.
I weave in the loose ends with a tapestry needle, going through the back of the fabric.
I block the finished piece by soaking it in water and pinning it to a towel to dry flat.
I seam the shoulder edges together using a mattress stitch for an invisible join.
I wind a skein of yarn into a ball using a swift and a ball winder.
I store my needles and hooks in a fabric case sorted by size.
I follow the written instructions for short rows to shape the heel of the sock.
I check the row counter to see how many rows I have completed so far.
